metadata.description: Questions where naive systems fail due to specific, identifiable traps. Every question has a false assumption, hidden conflict, or policy violation that a less careful system would miss. Answers require advisor validation.

A.name: Impossible Timeline
A.description: Student asks for something that cannot be done given constraints

B.name: Hidden Prerequisite Violation
B.description: System does shallow prereq check and misses a deeper requirement

C.name: Policy Conflict
C.description: Student's plan violates a policy they don't know about

D.name: Course Availability Trap
D.description: Course exists in catalog but isn't offered when needed

E.name: Double-Counting / Requirement Ambiguity
E.description: Course counted for two requirements when policy doesn't allow it

F.name: False Premise
F.description: Student's question contains a factual error the system should correct

questions.persona_summary: CS 5th-year, entered Fall 2016, Academic warning, Math minor, 45 courses
questions.question: I want to complete both my CS degree and my Math minor by Spring 2026. I know I'm on academic warning, but I think I can handle a heavy load. Plan my remaining courses.
questions.false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: The student assumes this is feasible within their remaining time. Academic warning imposes a unit cap per semester. Combined with the number of remaining CS + Math minor courses and prerequisite chains that must be sequenced, completing everything by Spring 2026 is likely mathematically impossible.
questions.naive_system_response: A naive system would generate a plan cramming all remaining courses into 1-2 semesters, either silently exceeding the academic warning unit cap or violating prerequisite ordering by scheduling dependent courses in the same semester.
questions.correct_response: Completing both your CS degree and Math minor by Spring 2026 is not feasible under your current academic warning status. The unit cap limits you to [X] units per semester, but you have [Y] remaining courses totaling approximately [Z] units, with prerequisite chains requiring at minimum [N] semesters. Your options: (1) drop the Math minor and focus on completing CS by Spring 2026, (2) extend to Fall 2026 to complete everything, (3) petition the dean for an academic warning unit cap exception with a strong rationale.
questions.why_multi_agent_helps: The Planning Agent would propose a plan. The Policy Agent would immediately flag the academic warning unit cap violation. The Programs Agent would confirm the full list of remaining requirements. The Courses Agent would verify prerequisite chains require more semesters than available. The proposal-critique protocol forces these checks before any plan is finalized — a single agent is likely to generate a plan without triggering the policy check.
key_facts: P-046 is on academic warning with a per-semester unit cap
P-046 entered in Fall 2016 — degree requirements may have changed
Remaining CS requirements + Math minor requirements exceed what fits in remaining semesters under the cap
Prerequisite chains impose a minimum number of sequential semesters
known_traps: Generating a plan that exceeds the academic warning unit cap
Scheduling courses that have prerequisite relationships in the same semester
Ignoring that the student has been enrolled since 2016 — catalog year issues
Not offering alternatives when the request is infeasible
questions.advisor_validation_needed: Verify: (1) exact academic warning unit cap from policy data, (2) exact remaining CS and Math minor requirements by auditing P-046's 45 courses against current requirements, (3) prerequisite chain lengths for remaining courses, (4) whether the impossibility is genuine

questions.persona_summary: CS 5th-year, no minor, 52 courses, Academic warning
questions.question: I absolutely must graduate by the end of this semester. What courses can I take right now to finish my CS degree?
questions.false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: The student assumes all remaining requirements can be completed in a single semester. With academic warning unit cap, if they have more remaining units than the cap allows, single-semester graduation is impossible regardless of course availability.
questions.naive_system_response: A naive system would list all remaining required courses and schedule them for the current semester without checking if the total units exceed the academic warning cap, or without verifying all courses are offered this semester.
questions.correct_response: Based on your course history, you still need [X] courses totaling approximately [Y] units. Your academic warning status limits you to [Z] units this semester. Since [Y] > [Z], completing everything this semester is not possible. You need at minimum [N] more semesters. Here is a plan that gets you to graduation as quickly as possible while respecting your unit limit: [semester-by-semester plan].
questions.why_multi_agent_helps: A single agent might list remaining courses without calculating total units against the warning cap. The Policy Agent specifically checks unit limits, the Programs Agent identifies remaining requirements, and the coordinator synthesizes these into a feasibility assessment before the Planning Agent attempts a plan.
key_facts: P-009 is on academic warning
Academic warning imposes a unit cap per semester
P-009 has taken 52 courses but may still have gaps
Single-semester completion requires all remaining units to fit under the cap
known_traps: Listing all remaining courses without checking unit total against cap
Not verifying course availability in the current semester
Assuming 52 courses means the student is almost done — they may have taken courses that don't count
questions.advisor_validation_needed: Verify: (1) exact remaining CS requirements for P-009, (2) academic warning unit cap, (3) whether single-semester completion is genuinely impossible, (4) optimal multi-semester path

questions.persona_summary: BA Senior, Entrepreneurship concentration, dual minors CS + International Relations, 47 courses, Good standing
questions.question: I'm a senior and I need to finish my Entrepreneurship concentration, my CS minor, and my International Relations minor by Spring 2026. Plan everything out for me.
questions.false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: Three areas of study with independent requirement sets. The CS minor alone has a long prerequisite chain. Combined with Entrepreneurship courses and IR minor courses, the total remaining load almost certainly exceeds what fits in 1-2 remaining semesters, especially if CS minor prereqs haven't been completed yet.
questions.naive_system_response: A naive system would generate a plan listing all remaining courses across three programs without recognizing that the CS minor prerequisite chain alone may require 2-3 more semesters, making Spring 2026 impossible.
questions.correct_response: Completing all three programs by Spring 2026 is extremely tight and likely not feasible. Your CS minor has a prerequisite chain that requires [N] sequential semesters, and you still need [X] IR minor courses and [Y] Entrepreneurship courses. Realistically, you need to either: (1) drop one of the two minors and complete the other on time, (2) extend by 1-2 semesters, or (3) petition for course substitutions if any overlap exists. Here's what each option looks like: [comparison].
questions.why_multi_agent_helps: The Programs Agent checks three separate requirement sets. The Courses Agent traces the CS minor prerequisite chain and determines minimum semesters needed. The Policy Agent checks unit limits. When the Planning Agent's proposal inevitably violates one of these, the parallel critique catches it — whereas a single agent might miss the prereq chain length while focusing on fitting courses into slots.
key_facts: P-056 has three separate program requirement sets to complete
CS minor for non-CS students has a strict, multi-semester prereq chain
Entrepreneurship concentration has limited course offerings
Total remaining courses likely exceed what's possible by Spring 2026
known_traps: Generating a plan without checking CS minor prereq chain length
Assuming all remaining courses can be taken in parallel when prereqs prevent it
Not recognizing that three programs competing for the same schedule slots creates infeasibility
questions.advisor_validation_needed: Verify: (1) remaining CS minor requirements and prereq chain depth for P-056, (2) remaining IR minor requirements, (3) remaining Entrepreneurship requirements, (4) whether any overlap exists between the three, (5) confirm impossibility or tight feasibility

questions.persona_summary: IS 5th-year, no concentration, no minor, entered Summer 2016, 47 courses, Good standing
questions.question: I've been enrolled since 2016 and I still don't have a concentration. I want to declare Data Science and graduate by Spring 2026. What's my plan?
questions.false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: Declaring Data Science concentration this late means the student likely hasn't completed DS-specific prerequisites. The DS prereq chain plus remaining core IS requirements may not fit in the remaining time. Additionally, IS program requirements have likely changed since 2016 — some completed courses may no longer count.
questions.naive_system_response: A naive system would accept the DS declaration and build a plan from the current DS requirements without checking whether courses taken years ago still count, or whether the DS prereq chain fits in the remaining timeline.
questions.correct_response: Declaring Data Science at this point is risky. You need [X] DS-specific courses with a prerequisite chain requiring at least [N] semesters. Given your remaining time, this may not be feasible. Also, since you entered in 2016, we need to audit which of your 47 courses still satisfy current IS requirements — some may have changed. I recommend: (1) meet with an advisor for an official degree audit, (2) consider whether completing IS without a concentration (if permitted) is faster, (3) if you must have a concentration, check which one you're closest to based on courses already taken.
questions.why_multi_agent_helps: The Programs Agent would flag that the DS concentration requires specific courses the student hasn't taken. The Courses Agent would trace the prereq chain and calculate minimum semesters. The Policy Agent would raise catalog year concerns for a student enrolled since 2016. A single agent might simply build a plan from current DS requirements without raising these structural issues.
key_facts: P-052 entered Summer 2016 — 10 years of enrollment
No concentration declared despite 47 courses
DS concentration has specific prerequisites with chain dependencies
IS requirements have likely changed since 2016
known_traps: Building a plan without auditing old courses against current requirements
Ignoring catalog year issues for a student enrolled since 2016
Not calculating whether DS prereq chain fits in remaining time
Not suggesting the student check which concentration requires fewest new courses
questions.advisor_validation_needed: Verify: (1) current DS concentration requirements, (2) which of P-052's courses satisfy current IS requirements, (3) catalog year policy for long-enrolled students, (4) whether DS is genuinely infeasible or merely tight, (5) which concentration P-052 is closest to

questions.persona_summary: BA 5th-year, Strategic Management, Psychology minor, 60 courses, Good standing
questions.question: I have a job starting in June 2026 and I absolutely cannot extend past Spring 2026. I think I have everything done but I want you to double-check and plan my final semester to be safe.
questions.false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: The student assumes they're essentially done with 60 courses. However, with a Psychology minor that has specific course requirements offered only in certain semesters, there may be a single remaining Psychology minor course that is NOT offered in Spring 2026 — meaning the student can't finish on time despite being 'almost done.'
questions.naive_system_response: A naive system would confirm 'you're almost done!' and list 1-2 remaining courses, possibly without checking whether those specific courses are actually offered in Spring 2026.
questions.correct_response: After auditing your 60 courses against BA + Strategic Management + Psychology minor requirements, you are missing [specific course(s)]. Unfortunately, [course X] for your Psychology minor is only offered in [Fall/specific semester], not Spring 2026. Your options: (1) find a substitute course that satisfies the same requirement and IS offered in Spring 2026, (2) petition for a course substitution, (3) take it during Summer 2026 before your job starts if timing permits.
questions.why_multi_agent_helps: The Programs Agent audits 60 courses and finds the gap. The Courses Agent verifies offering schedules and detects the availability problem. A single agent might confirm near-completion without cross-referencing the final requirement against the Spring 2026 schedule — missing the one course that's unavailable.
key_facts: P-029 has 60 courses — close to completion but not verified complete
Psychology minor has specific requirements that may not all be offered every semester
Job start date creates a hard deadline
One missing course in the wrong semester can derail graduation
known_traps: Assuming 60 courses means requirements are met without actually auditing
Confirming completion without checking Spring 2026 offering schedule
Not suggesting alternatives when the missing course isn't offered
questions.advisor_validation_needed: Verify: (1) exact remaining requirements after auditing 60 courses, (2) whether any remaining Psychology minor course is not offered Spring 2026, (3) whether a substitute exists, (4) summer course option timing relative to June job start

questions.persona_summary: BIO Junior, CS minor, 36 courses, Good standing
questions.question: I've taken 15-112 and I want to register for 15-213 next semester to make progress on my CS minor. Am I eligible?
questions.false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: 15-213 likely requires 15-122 (not just 15-112) as a prerequisite. The student has taken 15-112 but may have skipped 15-122. A shallow system might see '15-112 completed' and approve, not realizing 15-213 requires the intermediate course.
questions.naive_system_response: A naive system checks if the student has any CS course and approves: 'You've taken 15-112, you can register for 15-213.' It doesn't check that 15-213 requires 15-122 specifically, not just 15-112.
questions.correct_response: You cannot register for 15-213 yet. While you have completed 15-112, 15-213 requires 15-122 (Principles of Imperative Computation) as a prerequisite, which you have not taken. You need to take 15-122 first, then 15-213 the following semester. This means your CS minor will take at least 2 more semesters for this chain alone.
questions.why_multi_agent_helps: The Courses Agent specifically checks the full prerequisite list, not just whether any CS course is done. In the multi-agent system, the Courses Agent has a dedicated prompt to check ALL prerequisites, while a single-agent system processing a broad context may do a quick pattern match and miss the intermediate step.
key_facts: 15-213 requires 15-122 as prerequisite (not just 15-112)
P-036 has taken 15-112 but likely not 15-122
CS minor prerequisite chain: 15-112 → 15-122 → 15-213 → ...
known_traps: Checking only if the student has taken ANY CS course rather than the specific prerequisite
Confusing 15-112 with 15-122 — they sound similar but are different courses
Approving registration based on the student's stated intent rather than actual eligibility
questions.advisor_validation_needed: Verify: (1) exact prerequisites for 15-213, (2) whether P-036 has taken 15-122 from their course history, (3) the full CS minor prereq chain

questions.persona_summary: IS Junior, Data Science concentration, Tech Entrepreneurship minor, 35 courses, Good standing
questions.question: I want to take an advanced machine learning elective next semester. I've already completed the intro stats course. Am I ready?
questions.false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: Advanced ML courses typically require not just intro stats but also linear algebra and an intermediate programming course. The student mentions only stats. The system should check ALL prerequisites, not just the one the student mentions.
questions.naive_system_response: A naive system would check that the student has the stats prerequisite and approve: 'You've completed intro stats, you're eligible for the ML course.' It misses that the ML course also requires linear algebra and/or a programming course the student may not have taken.
questions.correct_response: The advanced ML elective requires: (1) intro statistics [✓ completed], (2) linear algebra [check if completed], and (3) intermediate programming/data structures [check if completed]. You're missing [specific courses]. You need to complete [X] before you can register for the ML course.
questions.why_multi_agent_helps: The Courses Agent retrieves the complete prerequisite list for the ML course, not just the one the student mentions. A single agent might anchor on the student's mention of stats and confirm that single prerequisite without checking the full list.
key_facts: Advanced ML courses typically have multiple prerequisites (stats + linear algebra + programming)
Student only mentions completing one prerequisite
IS students may not have taken math/CS courses that CS students would have
known_traps: Only checking the prerequisite the student explicitly mentions
Not retrieving the full prerequisite list from course data
Assuming IS students have the same math background as CS students
questions.advisor_validation_needed: Verify: (1) which advanced ML course exists at CMU-Q, (2) its full prerequisite list, (3) which prereqs P-015 has and hasn't completed

questions.persona_summary: BA Sophomore, Strategic Management, Tech Entrepreneurship minor, 31 courses, Good standing
questions.question: I'm interested in taking a data analytics course from the IS department to strengthen my Tech Entrepreneurship minor. Can I just sign up?
questions.false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: IS department courses often have IS-specific prerequisites (e.g., an intro IS course or specific programming course) that BA students haven't taken. The student assumes cross-department enrollment is straightforward, but prerequisite barriers may exist. Additionally, some courses may be restricted to IS majors.
questions.naive_system_response: A naive system might check if the course is offered and confirm availability without checking whether BA students can take IS courses or whether IS-specific prerequisites are satisfied.
questions.correct_response: The data analytics course [XX-XXX] has prerequisites: [specific IS courses]. As a BA student, you likely haven't taken [prerequisite course]. Additionally, check whether this course has a major restriction — some IS courses are reserved for IS students or require department permission. You would need to: (1) complete the prerequisite first, and (2) confirm enrollment eligibility for non-IS students.
questions.why_multi_agent_helps: The Courses Agent checks prerequisites. The Policy Agent checks enrollment restrictions by major. Together they catch both the prereq gap and the potential major restriction — a single agent might check one but not the other.
key_facts: IS courses may have IS-specific prerequisites BA students lack
Some courses have major/department enrollment restrictions
Cross-department enrollment often has hidden barriers
known_traps: Confirming a course exists without checking prerequisites for this specific student's background
Not checking major-restriction policies on the course
Assuming cross-department enrollment works the same as within-department
questions.advisor_validation_needed: Verify: (1) which data analytics courses exist in IS department, (2) their prerequisites, (3) whether P-024 has those prereqs, (4) any major restriction policies

questions.persona_summary: BIO Sophomore, Molecular Biology concentration, Neuroscience minor, 21 courses, Good standing
questions.question: I want to take an advanced neuroscience lab course for my minor. I've taken General Biology and the intro neuro course. Can I register?
questions.false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: Advanced lab courses often have hidden prerequisites beyond introductory courses — such as organic chemistry, biochemistry, or a specific methods course. The student assumes the intro sequence is sufficient, but the lab course likely requires additional preparation the student hasn't completed.
questions.naive_system_response: A naive system checks that the student has 'intro neuro' and 'General Biology' and approves, not realizing the lab course requires an intermediate course (e.g., biochemistry or a methods course) that the student hasn't taken.
questions.correct_response: The advanced neuroscience lab [XX-XXX] requires: (1) intro neuroscience [✓], (2) General Biology [✓], and (3) [specific intermediate course like biochemistry or research methods] which you have not yet completed. You need to take [intermediate course] first, which is offered in [semester].
questions.why_multi_agent_helps: The Courses Agent retrieves all prerequisites including non-obvious ones like intermediate chemistry requirements for biology lab courses. A single agent might pattern-match on 'neuro' prerequisites and miss the chemistry/methods requirement.
key_facts: Advanced lab courses often have prerequisites beyond the introductory sequence
Biology lab courses may require chemistry or methods courses
Sophomore students often haven't completed all intermediate prerequisites
known_traps: Only checking the 'obvious' neuro prerequisites and missing chemistry/methods requirements
Approving based on the student's description rather than the full prereq list
Not distinguishing between lecture courses and lab courses which often have different prereqs
questions.advisor_validation_needed: Verify: (1) which advanced neuro lab courses exist, (2) their full prerequisite lists including non-obvious ones, (3) what P-060 has and hasn't completed

questions.persona_summary: CS Junior, dual minors Math + SCS Computer Systems, 32 courses, Good standing
questions.question: I've completed 15-213 and I want to take the operating systems course next semester. I should be good on prereqs, right?
questions.false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: Operating systems courses may have prerequisites beyond just 15-213 — potentially requiring concurrent enrollment in or prior completion of a specific math course, or another systems course. The student assumes 15-213 alone is sufficient.
questions.naive_system_response: A naive system confirms: '15-213 completed, you're eligible for operating systems.' It doesn't check for additional prerequisites like concurrent math or a different systems prerequisite.
questions.correct_response: The operating systems course requires: (1) 15-213 [✓ completed], and (2) [additional prerequisite — check course data]. You are [eligible/not eligible] because [specific reason]. Note: this course may also have a corequisite requirement for [course] that must be taken simultaneously.
questions.why_multi_agent_helps: The Courses Agent checks ALL prerequisites including corequisites. A single agent processing the question might focus on the main prerequisite (15-213) and miss corequisite or secondary requirements.
key_facts: Systems courses often have multiple prerequisites and sometimes corequisites
15-213 is necessary but may not be sufficient
Corequisites (courses taken simultaneously) are easy to miss
known_traps: Confirming eligibility based only on the most obvious prerequisite
Missing corequisite requirements
Not distinguishing between prerequisites (taken before) and corequisites (taken simultaneously)
questions.advisor_validation_needed: Verify: (1) exact prerequisites for the OS course at CMU-Q, (2) whether any corequisites exist, (3) whether P-042 satisfies all of them

questions.persona_summary: IS Sophomore, no concentration, Academic warning, 25 courses
questions.question: I want to take 6 courses next semester to catch up and get back on track. I know it's a lot but I'm motivated. Can you build me an intensive schedule?
questions.false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: Academic warning policy limits the number of units a student can take per semester. Six courses would total approximately 54-72 units, almost certainly exceeding the academic warning cap. The student's motivation doesn't override policy.
questions.naive_system_response: A naive system builds an intensive 6-course schedule, optimizing for the student's stated goal of catching up. It doesn't check the academic warning unit restriction and produces a plan the registrar would reject.
questions.correct_response: I understand you want to catch up, but your academic warning status limits you to [X] units per semester. Six courses would total approximately [Y] units, exceeding this limit. You can take a maximum of [N] courses. Here's an optimized [N]-course schedule for next semester that prioritizes your most important requirements: [plan]. To fully catch up, here's a multi-semester recovery plan: [extended plan].
questions.why_multi_agent_helps: The Policy Agent immediately flags the academic warning unit cap before any plan is built. In a single-agent system, the 'catch up' framing biases the agent toward building an intensive schedule, and the policy check may never be triggered.
key_facts: P-013 is on academic warning
Academic warning imposes a unit cap per semester
Six courses would exceed the cap
Student motivation doesn't override academic policy
known_traps: Building an intensive schedule without checking unit cap policy
Optimizing for the student's stated goal without checking constraints
Not explaining WHY the limitation exists and HOW to work within it
questions.advisor_validation_needed: Verify: (1) exact academic warning unit cap, (2) typical units for 6 IS courses, (3) maximum number of courses allowed under the cap

questions.persona_summary: BA Junior, dual concentration Finance + BAT, Econ minor, 37 courses, Good standing
questions.question: My schedule is so tight with dual concentrations and a minor. I want to request an overload for next semester — can I take 7 courses? What should my schedule look like?
questions.false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: Overload requests typically require meeting a minimum GPA threshold (e.g., 3.5+) and advisor approval. The student assumes overload is just a matter of requesting it. If their GPA is below the threshold, the request would be denied.
questions.naive_system_response: A naive system builds a 7-course schedule and says 'you'll need to request an overload approval.' It doesn't check whether the student meets the GPA requirement for overload or what the approval process entails.
questions.correct_response: Overload requests at CMU-Q require a minimum GPA of [X] and advisor approval. Your current GPA is [check]. If you meet the threshold, here's a potential 7-course schedule: [plan]. However, I'd recommend considering whether [alternative plan with 5-6 courses + summer] might be less risky. If you don't meet the GPA threshold, overload won't be approved and you'll need to: [alternative plan].
questions.why_multi_agent_helps: The Policy Agent checks the overload GPA threshold before the Planning Agent builds a schedule. A single agent might build the 7-course plan first and mention the overload policy as an afterthought, or not at all.
key_facts: Overload requires minimum GPA threshold
Overload requires advisor approval
7 courses is well above normal load
Alternative approaches (summer courses, adjusted sequencing) may be safer
known_traps: Building an overload schedule without checking GPA eligibility
Treating overload approval as guaranteed
Not presenting alternatives to overloading
questions.advisor_validation_needed: Verify: (1) exact overload policy including GPA threshold, (2) P-025's GPA or standing, (3) maximum units allowed in overload, (4) approval process

questions.persona_summary: CS 5th-year, Tech Entrepreneurship minor, 41 courses, Good standing
questions.question: I need to take 3 courses this summer to graduate on time. My job offer starts in September so I need to be done by August. Plan my summer schedule.
questions.false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: Summer sessions typically have unit/course limits that are lower than regular semesters. Taking 3 courses in summer may exceed the summer unit cap. Additionally, not all courses are offered in summer, and summer sessions may be shorter, meaning course availability is limited.
questions.naive_system_response: A naive system schedules 3 courses in summer without checking summer-specific unit limits or course availability, producing a plan that may not be possible.
questions.correct_response: Summer sessions at CMU-Q have a unit limit of [X] units. Three courses would total approximately [Y] units. If this exceeds the limit, you can take a maximum of [N] courses in summer. Additionally, check which of your remaining courses are actually offered in summer — options are typically limited. Here's a feasible plan: [summer courses] + [remaining courses in a different term if needed].
questions.why_multi_agent_helps: The Policy Agent catches the summer unit limit. The Courses Agent checks which courses are offered in summer sessions. A single agent might assume summer works like a regular semester and build an infeasible plan.
key_facts: Summer sessions have different unit limits than regular semesters
Not all courses are offered in summer
Summer sessions may have shorter duration affecting scheduling
Job start date creates a hard deadline
known_traps: Treating summer like a regular semester for planning purposes
Not checking summer-specific unit caps
Not verifying summer course offerings
Scheduling courses that aren't offered in summer
questions.advisor_validation_needed: Verify: (1) summer unit cap from policy data, (2) summer 2026 course offerings, (3) whether 3 summer courses is permitted, (4) P-010's exact remaining requirements

questions.persona_summary: BIO Senior, Psychology minor, 56 courses, Good standing
questions.question: I got a C- in a required Bio course last year. I want to retake it this semester to improve my GPA for grad school applications. Can I just re-register?
questions.false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: Course retake policies vary — there may be limits on how many courses can be retaken, how the grade replacement works (does the old grade stay on the transcript?), and whether a C- even qualifies for retake (some policies only allow retakes for D or F grades). The student assumes retaking is straightforward.
questions.naive_system_response: A naive system would say 'Yes, you can retake it' and add it to the schedule, without checking the specific retake policy, grade threshold, or GPA replacement rules.
questions.correct_response: CMU-Q's course repeat policy states [specific rules]. A C- [does/does not] qualify for retake under this policy. If eligible, the grade replacement works as follows: [explanation]. Note: [X specific implications — e.g., both grades may appear on transcript, or there's a limit on total retakes]. Before retaking, consider whether [alternative like additional courses to boost GPA] might be more efficient for your grad school application.
questions.why_multi_agent_helps: The Policy Agent specifically checks retake/repeat policies with their exact conditions. A single agent might provide generic advice about retaking without checking the specific grade threshold or replacement rules.
key_facts: Course retake policies have specific conditions (grade thresholds, limits on number of retakes)
Grade replacement mechanics vary by policy
A C- may or may not qualify for retake
Both grades may appear on transcript depending on policy
known_traps: Assuming all grades qualify for retake
Not checking the specific retake/repeat policy
Not explaining how grade replacement actually works
Not considering alternatives to retaking
questions.advisor_validation_needed: Verify: (1) exact course retake/repeat policy, (2) grade threshold for eligibility, (3) how grade replacement works on transcript, (4) any limit on total retakes allowed

questions.persona_summary: IS Sophomore, Data Science, HCI minor, 24 courses, Good standing
questions.question: I want to take a graduate-level HCI course that counts for my minor. My advisor in the HCI department said it's fine. Can you add it to my plan?
questions.false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: Undergraduate students taking graduate courses typically need formal permission, may have unit limits on graduate credits counting toward undergraduate degrees, and the course may not actually satisfy the minor requirement even if the HCI department approves enrollment. Multiple policies interact here.
questions.naive_system_response: A naive system accepts 'my advisor said it's fine' at face value and adds the course to the plan without checking undergraduate/graduate enrollment policies, unit counting rules, or whether the course actually satisfies the minor requirement.
questions.correct_response: Taking graduate courses as an undergraduate involves several policy checks: (1) formal permission process beyond departmental advisor approval — you may need registrar approval, (2) there may be a limit on graduate units counting toward your undergraduate degree, (3) the graduate course must be approved to satisfy your HCI minor requirement specifically — department approval for enrollment is not the same as degree requirement satisfaction. I recommend: [specific steps to verify all three].
questions.why_multi_agent_helps: The Policy Agent checks undergraduate-graduate enrollment policies. The Programs Agent verifies whether the graduate course satisfies the minor requirement. The Courses Agent checks prerequisites. Three separate checks that a single agent might collapse into 'advisor said it's fine, you're good.'
key_facts: Departmental advisor approval ≠ university-level permission for grad course enrollment
Graduate units may not automatically count toward undergraduate degree
Course satisfying enrollment eligibility ≠ course satisfying degree requirement
Multiple levels of approval may be needed
known_traps: Accepting 'my advisor said it's fine' without checking formal policies
Confusing enrollment permission with degree requirement satisfaction
Not checking graduate-undergraduate unit counting rules
Not distinguishing between departmental and university-level approvals
questions.advisor_validation_needed: Verify: (1) policy on undergraduates taking graduate courses, (2) unit counting rules for grad courses in undergrad degrees, (3) whether grad HCI courses satisfy the HCI minor requirement, (4) approval process

questions.persona_summary: IS Senior, ISP concentration, History minor, 46 courses, Good standing
questions.question: I need to take one more History elective to complete my minor. I'm planning to take it in Spring 2026. Which History courses are available?
questions.false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: History courses at CMU-Q have limited and inconsistent offerings. The student assumes History electives will be available in Spring 2026, but the specific courses needed for the minor may only be offered in Fall, or may not be offered at all in 2025-2026.
questions.naive_system_response: A naive system pulls History courses from the catalog and lists them as options without checking the Spring 2026 schedule. The student gets a list of courses that don't actually exist next semester.
questions.correct_response: Looking at the Spring 2026 schedule, the following History courses are actually offered: [list from schedule data]. Of these, [X] satisfy your History minor requirement.
